column1: Table 1 — graded entries. Every row below was read from the primary source. Residue numbering, affinities and control statements are as reported there. On the disease composition of this set: nine of the fourteen targets are cancer-associated — MDM2, p27Kip1, the androgen receptor activation domain and AF1, c-Myc, the p53 transactivation domain, NUPR1, EWS-FLI1 and the p53/FOXO4-DRI entry — as are three of the four Tier A targets, which is why the title names cancer proteins. The remaining entries are retained deliberately rather than as strays: α-synuclein, amyloid-β 42 and tau are the most intensively studied disordered targets anywhere and set the standard of evidence the oncology entries are graded against, and the hepatitis C virus NS5A entry carries one of the four constraints of §4 — the only measurement in the curation showing a bound ligand that is not held in a fixed pose. A set restricted to cancer targets would have lost that constraint.

column3: EPI-001 and its four stereoisomers; EPI-7170; compound 1aa
column4: Read in full. CSPs "small but highly reproducible" across residues 354–448, in three partially folded sub-regions; much smaller in Tau-1. No residue-level site assignable — synthetic peptides matching each sub-region (341–371, 391–414, 426–446) produce no change in the EPI-001 spectrum, so "residues 354-448 must simultaneously be present". No stereoselectivity: all four stereoisomers interact similarly. Authors state the perturbations are "more than what is expected for the binding of a small molecule" and may combine "direct and indirect" effects, and that their data "do not provide us with a mechanism of molecular recognition". Separately: intact MS shows Cys404 reacts fastest; 2025 intermolecular PREs and ¹³C-filtered/edited aromatic NOEs show EPI-001 increases intermolecular aromatic contacts near ³⁹⁶AWAAAAAAQ⁴⁰³
column5: none measured in the primary paper. Simulated only: 5.24 mM (EPI-002), 1.92 mM (EPI-7170); simulated dimerisation Kd 1.8 ± 0.3 → 1.0 ± 0.3 (EPI-002) → 0.30 ± 0.03 mM (1aa)

column1: NS5A-D2D3 (hepatitis C virus NS5A, disordered domains 2–3)
column4: Read in full. Binding established by ligand-detected ¹⁹F transverse relaxation (CPMG R₂), with ¹⁹F R₁, ¹⁹F CSP and ¹H DOSY diffusion fitted simultaneously to a one-site model. Protein-detected CSPs are near-undetectable — largest under 12 ppb, at A308, W312, A313, T334, S414, S448 — and the authors state the subtle 1D changes "could have easily been mistaken for mismatched buffers", so no residue-level map is claimable. Crowding excluded by a matched-molecular-weight PEG-20k comparator. CD shows loss of disorder at ≥100 µM; at 200 µM protein the shifts and both relaxation rates increase, so engagement of the less disordered state is tighter
column5: 260 ± 110 µM; k_off 800 ± 500 s⁻¹; τc bound 46 ± 10 ps vs 27.0 ± 1.3 ps free
column6: no pH control reported, but the authors cite the pH artefact themselves and their primary observable is not CSP; crowding controlled; no mutagenesis
column7: unassigned, and informatively so — not pocket-like (see §4), not remodelling at low concentration, oligomer-dependent at high concentration

column1: TREX1 α7–α8 loop (mouse TREX1; DEDDh exonuclease)
column2: intrinsically disordered α7–α8 loop, res 167–178, established as a DNA-binding SLiM; a disordered loop on a folded enzyme
column4: Read in full. X-ray crystal structures of the complexes — the only crystallographic residue-level localisation in this table — plus three apo structures under different conditions, and all-atom MD initiated from the complexes. Binding-coupled disorder-to-order transition, with the ordered loop conformation different from its DNA-bound structure. Binding pattern is multivertex clamping onto an ensemble of chemical-scale amphiphilic units the authors term amphicons, at two sites consistently seen in both structures and MD. Inhibitors obstruct TREX1 DNA binding; effect on nuclease activity validated in cancer cells. Site chosen away from the active site because the DEDDh catalytic residues are family-conserved
column5: no equilibrium constant — readout is an enzymatic IC50 from a gel assay, so this entry does not enter Table 3
column6: pH artefact not applicable (no NMR titration); no mutagenesis of the loop, which a complex structure makes confirmatory rather than necessary
column7: pocket-like (disorder-to-order), but with the ordered state inhibitor-dependent — see §4
